sourceChecks.title: Catching a falling knife: an analysis of circuit breakers in UK equity markets
sourceChecks.excerpt: liquidity is lower and spreads are wider after circuit breakers
sourceChecks.paraphrase: The FCA study analyzes order-book conditions and circuit-breaker events in UK equities, finding market-depth and spread patterns after triggering.
sourceChecks.limitations: A bounded UK sample does not establish a general causal micro-to-macro crash model, broad predictive power, or universally effective circuit-breaker design.
sourceChecks.searchQuery: FCA catching a falling knife circuit breakers UK equity markets 51 events

sourceChecks.searchQuery: SEC CFTC findings market events May 6 2010 liquidity withdrawal report

sourceChecks.title: Aggregate Confusion: The Divergence of ESG Ratings
sourceChecks.excerpt: Measurement contributes 56% of the divergence, scope 38%, and weight 6%.
sourceChecks.paraphrase: This empirical study decomposes divergence among six ESG rating providers using 709 underlying indicators; it reports that measurement and scope differences explain most observed rating divergence.
sourceChecks.limitations: It analyzes rating disagreement, not causal links between ESG actions, risk premia, or real-world outcomes; no audit-ready universal pricing framework or investment scale is established.
sourceChecks.searchQuery: Berg Koelbel Rigobon Aggregate Confusion divergence ESG ratings 2022

sourceChecks.title: Asset Pricing Restrictions on Predictability: Frictions Matter

sourceChecks.limitations: Results are sample/model-specific and do not provide a universal information-theoretic upper bound on market predictability or alpha.
sourceChecks.searchQuery: predictable stock returns transaction costs frictions limits asset pricing paper

sourceChecks.title: The Limits of Arbitrage

innovations.summary: Factor models and empirical studies explain or organize subsets of return patterns; the cited NBER study documents extensive factor proliferation and data-mining risk. The source set does not establish one parsimonious theory explaining all named anomalies.

claims.claim: A single, parsimonious model accounting for equity premium, value/growth, momentum, low-volatility, profitability, and investment anomalies.
claims.scope: A published study identifies hundreds of reported factors and warns of multiple-testing/data-mining concerns; frictions work illustrates model-dependent reconciliation of some return predictability.
claims.limitations: Cannot show one model jointly explains equity premium, value, momentum, low volatility, profitability, and investment without ad-hoc factors; risk-adjusted performance and regulatory impacts are not demonstrated.

claims.claim: Claimed impact: Ends decades of factor-model proliferation and allows true risk-adjusted performance measurement.
claims.scope: No support established in this bounded source check for the stated impact.
claims.limitations: The cited result is narrower than the forecast impact; causal effectiveness, universal scale, and the projected economic outcomes are not established.

evidence.limitations: Does not supply a unified theory.
